PVE34 established a valid historical Nyx tuning point: the 200k 10M-crossing run completed cleanly at roughly 403 PGCR/sec steady and 408/sec late, with ample CPU idle. Its bottleneck was DB/write coordination, and PVE34 was preferable to PVE36 in that workload because it avoided the handler-commit/iowait cliff. It did not establish a universal worker configuration.

The later autonomy work superseded that fixed-shape operating model. Scenario-aware control exceeded 1k/sec in normal alpha backparse, reached about 2.24k/sec steady with parser-owned S3 in gamma, expanded fetch under beta latency, and contracted toward four workers at the slow edge. Worker counts became measured, reversible decisions; batch 128 became a keeper ceiling rather than a law; DB-lane changes became scenario-specific fixed-budget trials with rollback.

Correctness remains anchored in DB truth. Raw marker commits travel with summaries, autoscaler state is never correctness state, and ordinary parser restart must fill gaps without rebuild, replay, or special repair modes. Cortex cannot write through the parser DB path, parser-owned S3 reads remain in the fetch path, D2 protected Redis is read-only, and bounded runs must pass contiguous coverage, zero failed rows, S3/readback, cache-tail, observability, host-health, and clean-process gates.

The safest next experiment is a bounded, production-style longer alpha soak starting from learned priors without operator worker/lane hints. Observe host and MySQL pressure, hot-lane loading, queues, retries, controller decisions, and rollback behavior; then hard-kill and recover through a normal restart from DB truth. This is proposed work, not a verified result. A durable checkpoint was committed as `checkpoint:019f5635-2cf5-7dc0-a7e5-c6d40ec3a803`.

answer.answer: Safe checkpoint: keep the cloud-authoritative personal instance physically separate from the work instance. Automate only signed, encrypted, application-layer replication from a personal outbox into a work-local replica. The work side must have no route, credentials, or write capability to the personal service, and must perform retrieval and indexing locally. Nothing derived from work may return automatically. A recommendation may enter personal context only after explicit human-reviewed declassification, followed by an authorized evidence-backed, versioned workspace write. The read-only retrieval interface remains distinct from checkpoint, revision, and handoff writes.

claims.value: Personal memory and OpenAI work memory must reside in physically separate trust-domain instances. The personal cloud service is authoritative; the work agent operates on a separate work-local personal replica. This is an application-layer one-way boundary, not a claimed physical data diode.

The only allowed automated direction is personal-to-work: the personal cloud publishes signed, encrypted, versioned snapshots or deltas through a one-way outbox to a read-only work importer, which maintains and indexes a local replica. The importer has no route, credential, or write capability for the personal service.

No work query, prompt, search string, request body, embedding, output, error, telemetry, acknowledgement, access-log data, or other work-derived state may flow to the personal service. Imported personal objects are tagged with personal provenance and are non-exportable and non-promotable into ordinary work memory by default.

A work-generated recommendation may enter personal context only through a separate, explicit, human-reviewed declassification step. After approval, persistence uses the authorized write system: evidence-backed atomic saves that create immutable records and versions, with versioned checkpoint, revision, and handoff updates. This write model is separate from the stateful, snapshot-pinned, read-only retrieval interface; opening or querying a retrieval session does not create memory.
